title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 88-89): X is a stratified space, here aimed at the Deligne-Mumford compactification of M_{g,nu} and its boundary at infinity, with strata X_i and closures X̄_i. On p. 88 Grothendieck defines the following:
- A 'diagramme' of length nu of a global stratification is a chain of strata closures X̄_{i0} ⊂ X̄_{i1} ⊂ ... ⊂ X̄_{i_nu}; it is strict if the inclusions are strict.
- A 'local strict diagram' is a pair (x, Σ_*) with x in the open stratum X_{i0}, not merely in its closure.
- The set of such pairs is topologised by fixing Σ_* and letting x vary in open subsets of X_{i0}. This gives a space D^*_{Δ_r}.

This page:
1. The projection (x, Σ_*) ↦ x gives (301) D^*_{Δ_r} → X, which he calls a local immersion. The margin adds that the images of the connected components of D_{Δ_r} are the strata.
2. He then remarks that what this really encodes on X is only the local stratification induced by the global one. One could define it directly from the local structure using 'drapeaux en germes de strates' (flags of germs of strata at x). That is: replace global flags of closures by flags of local branches/germs of strata at the point x.
3. Test case: a normal-crossings divisor on an analytic space. Here the germ-flag construction recovers the coverings from the two preceding sections, D^*_{Δ_r} = ⨿_{d_r ∈ Δ_{r+1}(W)} D^*_{d_r}. These are essentially the normalisations of the r-fold self-intersection loci, i.e. points together with a choice of local branches.
4. He wants specialisation maps D^*_{Δ_r} → D_{Δ_{r'}} for face maps Δ_{r'} → Δ_r. On p. 89 he obtains them by allowing non-strict / closure-based diagrams (x ∈ X̄_{i0}). The open part D^*_{Δ_r} sits as a canonical open subset of D_{Δ_r}, and the D_{Δ_r} assemble into a semi-simplicial ('1/2 simplicial') space over X.

In modern terms: for an arbitrary stratified space he builds a semi-simplicial space of pointed flags of local strata germs, with each level mapping to X by a local immersion. This generalises Deligne's semi-simplicial resolution of a normal-crossings divisor by normalised multiple loci. It is closely related to the space of simplices of the exit-path category of the stratification, and to resolving the boundary of the compactified moduli space into its normalised boundary strata (indexed by stable graphs).
errors: With the topology literally as stated (global strata, Σ fixed, x varying in X_{i0}), each component of D^*_{Δ_r} is just a copy of the stratum X_{i0}. The map to X is then piecewise a locally closed embedding and cannot see local branches when stratum closures are not locally unibranch. Grothendieck himself notices this ('en fait ... stratification locale'), and switching to germs of strata is the needed correction.
Calling D → X a 'local immersion' is right only in the sense of locally closed embeddings on pieces; the map is not étale or a covering onto X. This is a terminological looseness, not a real gap.
The indexing ⨿_{d_r ∈ Δ_{r+1}(W)} (with Δ_r versus Δ_{r+1}) is ambiguous in the manuscript and depends on the conventions of the previous sections.

ideas.what: Space of pointed flags of strata (x, X̄_{i0} ⊂ ... ⊂ X̄_{iν}), with x in the smallest open stratum, mapping to X
ideas.modern_name: space of r-simplices of the exit-path / entrance-path category of a stratified space; nerve of the stratification poset with points
ideas.usually_credited_to: MacPherson (exit paths, unpublished c. 1990s); Treumann 2009; Lurie, Higher Algebra appendix A; Ayala-Francis-Tanaka
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses stratified 'tame' spaces and the boundary structure of M_{g,n} only qualitatively

ideas.what: Define diagrams via flags of germs of strata at x, giving the local stratification rather than the global one
ideas.modern_name: local branches / normalisation of strata; locally-defined stratification poset (sheaf of posets)
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard in stratification theory (Thom-Mather); for normal crossings, Deligne (Hodge II/III)

ideas.what: Recovering, for a normal-crossings divisor, the coverings D^*_{d_r} (normalised r-fold loci with choice of branches)
ideas.modern_name: Deligne's semi-simplicial resolution of an NCD; normalised boundary strata of DM-type compactifications

ideas.what: Specialisation maps from open to closed diagram spaces making the D_{Δ_r} a semi-simplicial space over X (continued p. 89)
ideas.modern_name: semi-simplicial space / simplicial resolution of a stratified space; face maps of exit-path nerve

missed.claim: For a general stratified space, Grothendieck proposes a canonical semi-simplicial space of pointed flags of germs of strata, each level mapping to X by a local immersion. It generalises Deligne's NCD resolution and anticipates the topological model of the exit-path category's nerve. He applies it to the boundary of the compactified moduli space M_{g,nu} to describe its 'structure at infinity'.
missed.quote: on pourrait la définir directement en termes de la structure locale à l'aide de la notion de "drapeaux en germes de strates"
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is an early, explicit point-set version of the exit-path / stratified-homotopy-type construction, motivated by moduli of curves. It links Esquisse-style 'structure à l'infini' to modern stratified homotopy theory, e.g. the combinatorics of tropical moduli and boundary complexes of M_{g,n}. It is of historical interest; the mathematics itself has since been developed independently.

deep.surprise_reason: The construction is natural and later developed independently (Deligne's resolution, exit-path categories). What is notable is seeing Grothendieck sketch a general germ-flag semi-simplicial resolution for stratified spaces in the M_{g,nu} context, but it is not a finished new result.
transcription_corrections: 'à l'aide de la notion de "des germes en germes de strates"' should most likely read 'à l'aide de la notion de "drapeaux en germes de strates"'.

'stratification à croisements[?] diviseurs : cv. norm.[?] associé à un diviseur' is a confused rendering of 'stratification associée à un diviseur à croisements normaux (cr. norm.) sur un espace analytique'.

'on exprime sur X une diagramme[?]' should probably read 'on n'emploie/n'exprime sur X des diagrammes que dans la stratification locale ...'; the inserted word is 'structurée'/'structure' above 'stratification locale'.
'on pourrait par la définir directement' should read 'on pourrait la définir directement'.
The formula appears as D^*_{Δ_r} = ⨿_{d_r ∈ Δ_{r+1}(W)} D^*_{d_r}, followed by 'des D_{Δ_r} des deux sections précédentes'.
